(Paterson, New Jersey) | college = [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] (2003–2007) | draft_year = 2007 | career_start = 2007 | career_end = 2020 | career_number = 13, 31 | career_position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] | years1 = {{nbay|2007|start}} | team1 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years2 = 2007–2008 | team2 = [[South Bay Lakers|Los Angeles D-Fenders]] | years3 = 2008 | team3 = [[Iowa Energy]] | years4 = 2008–2009 | team4 = [[Tianjin Ronggang]] | years5 = 2010–2011 | team5 = [[Hekmeh BC|Sagesse]] | years6 = 2011–2012 | team6 = [[ETHA Engomis]] | years7 = {{nbay|2011|end}} | team7 = [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]] | years8 = 2012–2013 | team8 = [[PBC Lukoil Academic|Lukoil Academic]] | years9 = 2013–2014 | team9 = [[Spirou Charleroi|Spirou]] | years10 = 2014–2015 | team10 = [[Reims Champagne Basket|Chalons-Reims]] | years11 = 2015–2018 | team11 = [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] | years12 = 2019–2020 | team12 = [[CLS Knights Indonesia|BTN CLS Knights Indonesia]] | highlights = * [[ASEAN Basketball League]] Champion (2019) * [[National Basketball League (Bulgaria)|Bulgarian League]] champion (2013) *2x [[LNB All-Star Game|French League All-Star]] ([[2015–16 LNB Pro A season|2016]], [[2016–17 LNB Pro A season|2017]]) }} '''Darryl Finesse Watkins''' (born November 8, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played for [[CLS Knights Indonesia|BTN CLS Knights Indonesia]] of the [[Asean Basketball League]]. He is a former [[college basketball]] player for the [[Syracuse Orange]] who has a reputation for his shot-blocking ability.{{cite web |title=Darryl Watkins Profile |first=Ray |last=Young |url=http://orangehoops.org/DWatkins.htm |work=Orangehoops.org |accessdate=2007-08-25}} ==High school== A first-team all-state pick as a senior, Watkins was a four-time all-county selection and earned all-area his final two seasons. He averaged approximately 16 points, 11 rebounds, six blocks and three assists in his senior campaign.{{cite web |title=Darryl Watkins Profile |url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=1458&sport=176&roster=194&path=mbasket |work=SUAthletics.com |accessdate=2007-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927191512/http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=1458&sport=176&roster=194&path=mbasket |archive-date=2007-09-27 |url-status=dead }} He was rated 35th nationally and seventh at center by ESPN.com, 35th by PrepStars, 51st by Insiders Hoops, and 60th by Hoop Scoop. New Jersey Hoops ranked him 4th in New Jersey. ==College== Used as a backup for his first two seasons at Syracuse, Watkins became Syracuse's starting center in his junior year. He registered 99 blocks that season, and ranked 16th in Division I blocked shots per game (2.8). He finished the season averaging 7.1 points and 7.3 rebounds.{{cite web |title=Darryl Watkins Prospect Profile |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/DarrylWatkins.html |work=NBA.com |accessdate=2007-08-25}} Watkins averaged 8.1 points and 7.5 rebounds a game in his senior year. He missed several games early on in the season due to a bruised nose, but still appeared in 33 games, starting 32 of them. He continued his intimidation inside, ranking seventh in Division I players in blocked-shot average (3.4). In the [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], Watkins blocked six shots against San Diego State,[https://web.archive.org/web/20120928113901/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270780183 Largest crowd in NIT history cheers Orange to second-round win] tying Syracuse's NIT record. Watkins wore # 13 as a member of the Orange. ===College legacy=== Watkins finished his career with 67 starts in 106 appearances with averages of 6.0 points and 5.8 rebounds per game. He ranked fifth in career blocks at Syracuse with 263 and recorded three or more blocks in a game 48 times during his tenure. Highlights include blocking a career-high 8 shots in a 67–62 win over [[Cornell University|Cornell]] on November 9, 2005,[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=253130183 Cornell 62, Syracuse 67 - Box score] and matching that with another 8-block effort in a 77–76 win over [[University of Cincinnati|Cincinnati]] on January 27, 2007.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120724035529/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270170183|title=Syracuse 77, Cincinnati 76}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings=== On June 29, 2007, Watkins signed a free agent contract with the Sacramento Kings. Watkins played for the Kings' mini-camp in early July and also in their Vegas summer league. In the Vegas summer league, he averaged 3.8 points, 3.4 rebounds and 0.8 blocks per game, including a nine-point, three-rebound effort against the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web |title=Darryl Watkins Profile |url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2007/players/index.jsp?player=darryl_watkins |work=NBA.com |accessdate=2007-08-25 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104053549/http://www.nba.com/summerleague2007/players/index.jsp?player=darryl_watkins |archivedate=2012-11-04 }} In August 2007, Watkins signed a partially guaranteed deal worth an estimated $450,000 with the Kings and appeared in nine games.{{cite web |title=Paterson alumni begin pro hoops careers |first=Adam |last=Zagoria |date=2007-08-12 |url=http://www.northjersey.com/page.php?qstr=eXJpcnk3ZjczN2Y3dnFlZUVFeXkxMzEmZmdiZWw3Zjd2cWVlRUV5eTcxODEzMzEmeXJpcnk3ZjcxN2Y3dnFlZUVFeXky |work=The Herald News |accessdate=2007-08-23}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}} ===D-League Stint (Iowa Energy and LA D-Fenders)=== On December 10, the Kings waived Watkins. Watkins split the rest of the season with the [[South Bay Lakers|Los Angeles D-Fenders]] and the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]].{{cite web |title=CNY in the Pros |url=http://blog.syracuse.com/cnypros/2007/12/weekly_nba_wrap.html |work=The Post Standard |date=5 December 2007 |accessdate=2007-12-16}} ===Los Angeles Clippers=== Watkins played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the 2008 Las Vegas Summer League.[http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2008/07/you_cant_spell_nba_summer_leag.html You can't spell NBA SUmmer League without SU - Orange Basketball Blog on syracuse.com] ===San Antonio Spurs=== On September 11, 2008, Watkins signed a two-year deal with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].[http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2008/09/darryl_watkins_set_to_sign_wit.html Darryl Watkins set to sign with San Antonio] He, along with [[Devin Green]] and [[Salim Stoudamire]], were cut on October 23.[http://www.nba.com/2008/news/10/23/102308knickscuthouston.ap/index.html?rss=true Roster roundup: Knicks waive Houston, ending comeback] ===Tianjin (CBA)=== When no [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] team signed Watkins, he signed with [[Tianjin Ronggang]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] on November 6, 2008.[http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2008/11/darryl_watkins_signs_with_chin.html Darryl Watkins signs with CBA team] ===2009–2010=== [[KK Crvena zvezda]] (BC Red Star Belgrade) agreed to sign Watkins for the 2009–10 season.[http://mtsmondo.com/sport/vesti/text.php?vest=149057 Darryl Watkins close to Red Star Belgrade] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091008113546/http://www.mtsmondo.com/sport/vesti/text.php?vest=149057 |date=2009-10-08 }} However, Watkins opted to remain in the United States after the birth of his daughter on August 14. He tried out for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]],Rick Noland. [http://chronicle.northcoastnow.com/2009/10/15/cavs-missing-some-key-ingredients-in-loss-to-wizards/ Cavs missing some key ingredients in loss to Wizards]. ''Chronicle Telegram''. October 15, 2009. Retrieved on October 15, 2009. but was waived on October 22, 2009.[http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/62291/20091022/cavs_waive_barrett_robinson_watkins/ Cavs Waive Barrett, Robinson, Watkins] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091024234301/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/62291/20091022/cavs_waive_barrett_robinson_watkins/ |date=2009-10-24 }} ===2010–2011=== Watkins played for the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[Orlando Pro Summer League]] in 2010. He then signed a contract with [[Hekmeh BC|Sagesse]] in the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/basketball.aspx?NewsID=209229|title=Lebanese Basketball, News, Teams, Scores, Stats, Standings, Awards - asia-basket}} ===2011–2012=== Watkins played with [[ETHA Engomis|Etha Engomis]] of Cyprus for 2011–12.[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.teamID_96279.compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2012.roundID_8593.coid_rjNSTmE3HHYlQ2HIPXkgY3.articleMode_on.html Triumph Suffer First Defeat To ETHA | EuroChallenge 2012 | FIBA Europe] The [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]] signed Watkins to a 10-day contract on April 18, 2012.[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/hornets-add-c-darryl-watkins-waive-ex-lsu-standout-chris-johnson/2012/04/18/gIQAy51hRT_story.html Hornets sign Watkins]{{dead link|date=June 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} In his first game with New Orleans, he recorded 13 rebounds (a game high) and 2 points in 29 minutes in a loss to Memphis.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201204180MEM.html|title = New Orleans Hornets at Memphis Grizzlies Box Score, April 18, 2012}} ===Philadelphia 76ers=== On July 11, 2012, Watkins was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in a three-team trade. The Sixers waived him just five days later, on July 16, after acquiring [[Kwame Brown]].{{cite web |url=http://www.csnphilly.com/basketball-philadelphia-sixers/sixers-talk/Sixers-waive-big-man-Darryl-Watkins?blockID=740854&feedID=704 |title=Sixers waive big man Darryl Watkins |accessdate=2012-07-16
